headline: Berry integration drives a swing back to profit

kpis.label: Net income
kpis.delta: swing to profit from a $39M loss

summary_short: Amcor's fiscal Q4 2026 net sales rose 26% y/y to $6,398 million, with adjusted EBITDA up 32% to $1,045 million and adjusted diluted EPS up 23% to $1.23.
summary_long: Net sales rose 26% y/y to $6,398M, driven mainly by the Berry Global acquisition (~19 pts) and pass-through of higher raw-material costs (~6 pts). Adjusted EBIT rose 37% on acquired earnings, Berry synergies (~$100M) and cost/productivity initiatives. GAAP net income swung to a $389M profit from a $39M year-ago loss as one-off Berry-deal transaction, merger-compensation, and inventory step-up charges present a year ago did not recur. Free cash flow rose 48% to $1,396M. The board declared a $0.65/share quarterly dividend. Amcor is transitioning its fiscal year-end from June 30 to December 31 and guided the resulting six-month Transition Period (Jul-Dec 2026) to adjusted EPS of $1.80-$1.90 and leverage of 3.5x-3.6x.
confidence_notes: Amcor's fiscal year ends June 30, so this release covers fiscal Q4 2026 (Apr-Jun); the shard files it under the calendar-quarter label FY2026 Q2. All prior-year figures reflect the combined Amcor/Berry Global entity from the April 2025 merger, and all share/EPS figures are retroactively adjusted for the 1-for-5 reverse stock split effected January 14, 2026. The company is also changing its fiscal year-end from June 30 to December 31, so the FY2026 Q2 label will not have a directly comparable next-quarter shard event — the next reporting period is a six-month 'Transition Period' ending December 31, 2026.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven mainly by the Berry Global acquisition (~19 points) and favorable pass-through of raw-material cost increases (~6 points), partly offset by a (1)% net volume/price-mix impact.
Swing to profit reflects the absence of one-off Berry-deal costs present a year ago (transaction costs, merger-related compensation, inventory step-up amortization) plus underlying EBIT growth.
Growth mainly reflects Berry acquisition synergy realization (~$100M) and strong execution on cost and productivity initiatives, including in non-core businesses.
Management cited strong operating performance despite a challenging macro backdrop, broad-based volume growth, effective input-cost management, and synergy capture running ahead of plan.
